fields.statement: Built rhiza from the branch head and drove it in a scratch git repo with real hold (wait) and slow/flaky (command) workflows. With a run stopped at a wait via --no-wait, a second run start (human, --json and --dry-run) exited 2 naming that run with next: rhiza run resume <id>, and no second journal appeared. A run whose process was SIGKILLed mid-step still blocked a new start, exit 2 naming it. Six concurrent run start processes on one change set: exactly one began (exit 0), five exited 2 naming it. With a failed run and a second run stopped at a wait, run resume --retry (and --dry-run) on the failed run exited 2 naming the second. Two concurrent resume --retry of two failed runs: one succeeded, the other exited 2 naming it. After the live run finished, a new start succeeded.

Built rhiza from the branch head and drove it in a scratch git repo. run abandon --dry-run on a run stopped at a wait printed 'would be abandoned' and left it stopped. run abandon by a 4+ char prefix journalled it failed with detail 'abandoned by <actor>' (run status human and --json); git worktree list and branch cs/<slug> still existed. run resume and run resume --retry on it exited 2 with 'was abandoned'; a second abandon exited 2 'is finished: it failed'. Abandon of a run running in another process exited 3 (running in another process). A SIGKILLed interrupted run was abandoned, after which run start on the change set succeeded and finished.
